criteria.text: `GET /api/people/lula/docs` (no `term`, default `days=30`) returns `total: 3, docs.length: 3`, matching `graphFor`'s existing `stats.about === 3` for Lula at `days=30`. — `test/docs.test.ts`
`docs` are ordered newest-first: for #1, `docs[0].published_at > docs[1].published_at > docs[2].published_at`. — `test/docs.test.ts`
`term=reforma&kind=bogus` returns the same `total: 2` as `kind=all` (unknown kind falls back to `all`). — `test/docs.test.ts`

`term=reforma&kind=word&limit=1&offset=0` then `offset=1` for Lula each return `docs.length: 1`, `total: 2` on both calls, and the two calls return different, correctly-ordered doc ids (newest first). — `test/docs.test.ts`
A doc from a non-GDELT source in the response always has `tone: null` — never a synthesized value. — `test/docs.test.ts`
A person with zero matching docs (empty window, e.g. `days=1` on a person whose only docs are older, or a person with no docs at all) returns `total: 0, docs: []`. — `test/docs.test.ts`

`GET /api/people/nobody/docs` returns HTTP 404 with `{ error: 'person not found' }` — checked the same way as the existing `/graph` and `/sources` routes (no dedicated HTTP-layer test exists for those either): manual step, `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' localhost:3210/api/people/nobody/docs` → `404`.
Clicking a hashtag/word/theme node in `public/design-5.html` opens `#docPanel` with that term's docs; clicking a person node does nothing. — manual step in the browser.
`Esc` and the panel's close button both hide `#docPanel`; `aside#sources` remains visible and interactive throughout. — manual step in the browser.
With zero matching docs, the panel shows the empty-state copy and no `carregar mais` button. — manual step in the browser.
README's API section lists the new route with its query params and response shape, in the same one-liner style as the existing three routes. — manual review of the README diff.
